bracket: [Textbook inconsistency between two entries of the same answer key. The printed key for Exercise 3.4 reads "Only (c) and (d) are permissible", which excludes THIS part — adding a component of a vector to the same vector. That exclusion only follows if "component" means the SCALAR coefficient \(A_x\), which would collapse this into case (b), adding a scalar to a vector. But the key for the very next question, Ex 3.5(b), marks "each component of a vector is always a scalar" as FALSE — i.e. a component IS a vector. Under that reading this operation adds a vector to another vector of the same dimensions and IS permissible. The chapter's own text agrees with the key's 3.5(b): §3.5 resolves \(\vec{A} = \lambda\vec{a} + \mu\vec{b}\) and calls \(\lambda\vec{a}\), \(\mu\vec{b}\) the COMPONENT VECTORS, and Eq. (3.16b) writes \(\vec{A} = A_x\hat{i} + A_y\hat{j} + A_z\hat{k}\). The two key entries cannot both be right under one definition of "component"; the answer below follows the vector reading and says so.]
